_comment: CASTABOT branding map. Ordered rule_sets -- earlier sets run first, so put
the longest / most specific tokens before the generic ones.
SCOPE: visible branding only. Identifiers, module names, env vars, the
`hermes` command and the ~/.hermes config dir are deliberately untouched --
renaming them is a rewrite of the product, not a rebrand, and it is the
single biggest source of upstream merge pain.
NEVER add a blanket lowercase `hermes` rule. Lowercase `hermes` is the CLI
command, the config dir and the npm scope; it must keep working.
NEVER rewrite `nousresearch.com` globally. It is not only branding:
`portal.nousresearch.com` and the TOOL_GATEWAY_DOMAIN are live third-party
HTTP-Referer header sent to inference providers. A global rewrite turns
them into github.com/castaso and silently breaks the product. URL branding
lives in the docs-only `doc_urls` rule set for exactly that reason.

protect.comment: Every copyright line naming Nous, including vendored third-party Apache headers. Rewriting a copyright notice is the one edit that can turn a lawful rebrand into a license violation.

templates.comment: Replaces upstream's README wholesale rather than token-swapping it: the upstream README is Nous's marketing copy, and a rebrand should not ship it under a new name.
Append-only. The MIT grant and the original 'Copyright (c) 2025 Nous Research' line above it are never edited -- MIT requires the notice to survive, and an edit would void the licence.

rule_sets.name: doc_urls
rule_sets.comment: URL rewriting is DOCS-ONLY. In a markdown file a URL is a link a reader clicks; in code it is a runtime endpoint or a provider header contract. Same literal, completely different blast radius.

rules.comment: The installer URLs are protected above: Nous still owns that host, so a fork cannot serve install.sh from GitHub Pages.
Docs-scoped only, so this cannot touch an API base URL. Links to the org in prose now point at the fork owner.

rule_sets.name: org_name
rule_sets.comment: SECURITY* is excluded on purpose: those documents route vulnerability reports, and the brand rule must not repoint them at a fork that runs no security process. CASTABOT README.md and NOTICE.md say so instead.

rules.comment: Spelled-out org name. Bare `NousResearch` is NOT rewritten -- it is the Hugging Face org for the Hermes-3/Hermes-4 model repos, the Windows installer staging prefix, and GitHub team handles like @NousResearch/hermes-agent-core.
Percent-encoded form, e.g. the shields.io badge label `Built%20by-Nous%20Research`. Without this the README badge keeps rendering the old brand next to the new alt text.

rule_sets.name: product_name
rule_sets.comment: Multi-word proper nouns. Safe in prose and in code string literals alike -- these are never identifiers, and both sides of a test assertion move together.

rule_sets.name: prose_product_name
rule_sets.comment: Standalone `Hermes` in markdown only. The digit guard keeps Hermes-3 / Hermes 4 model names intact; the word-boundary guards keep hyphenated identifiers and env vars out.

rules.comment: Possessive first -- otherwise the generic rule below yields `CASTABOT'`.

rule_sets.name: brand_code_strings
rule_sets.comment: Standalone `Hermes` in the runtime files whose text a user actually sees. Curated rather than extension-wide: a blanket sweep over .py would hit identifiers and dict keys.

rule_sets.name: site_config
rule_sets.comment: Docusaurus identity fields the generic rules do not reach: single-quoted, and `NousResearch`/`hermes-agent` as bare config values rather than inside a URL.
